rule: An assertion holds exactly what the recipe's declaration and the source documents together determine, no more and no less: what someone holding only the recipe, the documents and the assertion, never having seen a run, would write.

assertions.where: issues/q2.json filters state
assertions.why: state is a closed vocabulary, so eq on "confirmed" is exact.

assertions.where: issues/q2.json filters app_version
assertions.why: app_version is free text ("the app version the statement names") and the sources write "2.3" and "version 2.3", so only containment of 2.3 is determined.

assertions.where: issues/q2.json relations
assertions.assertion: case_state.subject -> case whose case.reporter is person mira
assertions.why: The reminder case is the one whose derived reporter is mira, so the relation picks it out by declared structure.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q2 expected_matched
assertions.why: comment-101-1 is the only maintainer statement confirming the bug, and it names 2.3; issue-101's 2.3 statement is a report, not a confirmation.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q2 row state.reminders.confirmed-2.3 type
assertions.why: q2 targets the declared claim kind case_state.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q2 row state.reminders.confirmed-2.3 attributes.state
assertions.why: "I can reproduce this ... this is a bug on our side" maps to confirmed and to no other declared value.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q2 row state.reminders.confirmed-2.3 attributes.app_version
assertions.to: app_version not asserted exactly; asserted by q2.json op contains "2.3" and by attribute_evidence
assertions.why: app_version is free text and "2.3", "version 2.3" or "v2.3" are all faithful; the scorer compares attributes only by equality.

assertions.assertion: comment-101-1: "The scheduler stores the reminder time twice when the offset moves, so this is a bug on our side."
assertions.why: "this is a bug on our side" itself confirms the case.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q2 row state.reminders.confirmed-2.3 refs subject
assertions.why: The comment is in thread 101 and speaks of the doubled reminders.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q2 row state.reminders.confirmed-2.3 attribute_evidence app_version
assertions.assertion: comment-101-1: "I can reproduce this on 2.3 with any reminder created before the change."
assertions.why: This is the sentence of the confirming comment that names the version.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q2 row state.reminders.confirmed-2.3 evidence
assertions.assertion: comment-101-1: "The scheduler stores ... bug on our side."
assertions.why: The confirmation is cited to the comment that makes it.

assertions.where: issues/q3.json filters app_version
assertions.why: app_version is free text and the source writes "version 2.4" and "2.4", so only containment is determined.

assertions.where: issues/q3.json relations
assertions.assertion: case_state.subject -> case whose case.reporter is person mira
assertions.why: It selects the reminder case by its derived reporter.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 expected_matched
assertions.why: Only comment-101-2 ("The fix ... is merged and goes out in version 2.4") is determined. comment-101-3's "Please update to 2.4 first." is an instruction whose case_state reading depends on context (the scorer's own semantic note says so), so the count is 1 or 2. The schema cannot express this.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 distinct_row_ids
assertions.why: If comment-101-3 yields a statement, it is a separate document's statement, and the scorer judges this only when both rows are bound.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 same_subject_id
assertions.why: Both comments are in thread 101 about the doubled reminders, and the scorer judges this only when every row is bound.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-2 type
assertions.why: q3 targets case_state.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-2 attributes.app_version
assertions.to: app_version not asserted exactly; asserted by q3.json op contains "2.4" and by attribute_evidence
assertions.why: The free-text app_version could be written "2.4" or "version 2.4" (the source's own words).

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-2 attributes.state
assertions.why: "The fix for the doubled reminders is merged" can only be resolved among reported/confirmed/resolved/declined, and leaving it unasserted would pass a wrong state.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-2 id_bind_from

assertions.to: comment-101-2: "The fix for the doubled reminders is merged and goes out in version 2.4 this week."
assertions.why: The post-update instruction does not state where the case stands; the fix sentence does.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-2 refs subject

assertions.why: This is the sentence that names 2.4.

assertions.assertion: comment-101-2: "After updating, open the app once ..."
assertions.to: comment-101-2: "The fix for the doubled reminders is merged and goes out in version 2.4 this week."
assertions.why: The instruction line is not a case_state statement; the resolution is.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-3 (presence)
assertions.assertion: a case_state row from comment-101-3 is required
assertions.why: "Please update to 2.4 first." is an instruction, and a reader may or may not read it as a resolved state. The schema has no optional row, so the row stays required.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-3 type
assertions.why: If present, the row is a case_state.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-3 attributes.app_version
assertions.to: app_version not asserted exactly; asserted by q3.json op contains "2.4" and by attribute_evidence
assertions.why: app_version is free text, so only containment of 2.4 is determined.

assertions.assertion: comment-101-3: "After updating, open the app once so that the scheduler can rebuild its list of reminders."
assertions.why: The repeated instruction states no case_state and names no version; the only sentence that could carry this row's state and 2.4 is "Please update to 2.4 first."

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-3 refs subject

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml query q3 row instruction.reminders.comment-101-3 attribute_evidence app_version

assertions.assertion: "Thanks, noted for the roadmap." yields no case_state
assertions.why: Noting a request for the roadmap neither confirms, resolves nor declines it, and "reported" was already stated by issue-102.

assertions.where: issues/expected.toml unknown case.reminders comment-101-4
assertions.assertion: "Thanks, all good now." yields no case_state
assertions.why: "all good now" faithfully reads as the reporter stating the case resolved, and equally as thanks that states nothing new, so neither a claim nor its absence is determined.

assertions.where: svrn/docs/cli-contract.toml journey layer-issues-default-path step corpus install stdout_contains
assertions.why: This is the CLI's install acknowledgement and does not read the documents.

assertions.where: svrn/docs/cli-contract.toml journey layer-issues-default-path step enrich init stdout_contains
assertions.why: The recipe declares [enrichment.ontology], so init selects the custom atlas.

assertions.where: svrn/docs/cli-contract.toml journey layer-issues-default-path step enrich extract stdout_contains
assertions.why: This is the CLI's extract acknowledgement.

assertions.where: svrn/docs/cli-contract.toml journey layer-issues-default-path step enrich resolve stdout_contains
assertions.why: case has an identity_criterion (RESOLVE decides it) and declares reporter derived = reporter_of_case, so the document step prints this line, which is the analogue of mailraw's asserted line; "RESOLVE" alone would pass a run that derived no reporter.

assertions.where: svrn/docs/cli-contract.toml journey layer-issues-default-path step q1 stdout_contains
assertions.why: There are exactly two cases.

assertions.where: svrn/docs/cli-contract.toml journey layer-issues-default-path step q2 stdout_contains
assertions.why: There is one confirmed state naming 2.3 (comment-101-1).

assertions.where: svrn/docs/cli-contract.toml journey layer-issues-default-path step q3 stdout_contains
assertions.why: The count is 1 or 2, depending on whether comment-101-3's instruction is read as a case_state. One stdout_contains string cannot express either-or, and a claim row prints the reader's content rather than the source quote, so the assertion is left unchanged.
